items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1995-11-14
items.q: And they had Willie Humphrey, Son Johnson.

ctx.x: Now how is he related to the other Baptists? Uh-uh.

Then they had Kerry Levine. Levine, okay. He was a saxophone player. And they had Willie Humphrey, Son Johnson. And my cousin, the one who played piano, she was teaching over there. What's your cousin's name? Margie.
Oh, Margie Dickerson? Yeah. She taught over there too. And she was that well-versed that she- Oh yeah.

items.title: Wallace Davenport Interview, 1975-05-15
items.q: The old Willie Humphrey, yeah. I knew him.

ctx.x: Where do you get your timing from? How do you learn timing? Well I had some very good instructors when I started out.

Now like this guy, Tull, old Professor Tull, he was a very good music teacher. He was a very good teacher. He took lessons from him too. The old Willie Humphrey. The old Willie Humphrey, yeah. I knew him. He was fine then. And I learned a lot from Alonzo Edson. See, I was teaching up there in Greenwood, but I was taking private lessons from him. Did you ever learn anything about listening to jazz musicians? Oh yeah. I learned a lot about listening to a Louis Armstrong role.
I was teaching up there in Greenwood, but I was taking private lessons from him.
